[ozchobie] Better off buying the sandisk microsd express discounted. More expensive but still cheap and I’d say better reliability for what it offers and could be backwards compatible speed wise. https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/977162
[Bal] Horses for courses. not great if you want one for 4K video recording on a action cam for example.
[ozchobie] Most, if not all consumer action cameras (current GoPro, DJI, insta360 models), cap at UHS1 write speeds anyways so there will be no difference in write speeds. Even those ones that feature 8k recording still caps write speeds to UHS1 standard.
[aligab] Action cam requirement is U3. V30 A2 like DJI drone or action cam
[Proliferation] You'd be surprised, there was a big roundup done recently on Micro SD endurance and among the models tested Amazon Basics was the only product line not to experience any failures:
https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/microsd-cards/mic…
Also, SD Express cards use more power (marginally) than micro SD/HC/XC cards even when inserted into a legacy host and running in backwards compatibility mode, so for things that don't support Express and situations where you aren't getting the benefit of the extra speed you might as well go with a cheaper micro SD card. Especially for devices running off a battery, like a smartphone/DAP/android handheld/etc.
[ozchobie] Ok that's a fairer case then if it does cause thermal and power issues due to fallback. Thanks for this info!
